sermon.title: The Seventh Trumpet Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins the seventh trumpet by critiquing popular prophecy charts, then teaches from Revelation 11 that the temple is the church, the new Jerusalem is the church, and the two witnesses cannot be anyone from history. He ends with the seventh trumpet and the reign of Christ.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: the captions give “Revelations 8:9 through 11:15” as he spoke it; it is left as spoken. The captions read “Paul” as “ax” in the Sinai aside (“why does Paul say it was in Arabia”), and “Acts 1:8” was spoken as “acts 1 18”. He gives “Galatians 4:25” twice, then reads on through verse 26. In the first minutes he speaks quickly about the premillennial, amillennial and postmillennial charts and the rapture views; these are his own criticisms as spoken. One short garbled spot between 2:57 and 4:40 is marked [unclear]. He also discusses Jerusalem, the Jewish temple and Israel, and says “good God, help us” about a temple being built; near the end he asks if “our government” is mad at Jesus.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say the end-time prophecy charts do not add up?
chunks.short_answer: He shows charts of the premillennial view and says the seals, trumpets, two witnesses, the man-child’s mother and the beast each get “three and a half years,” which “adds up to about 14 years, not seven.” He asks what the authors’ end goal is, and says “the whole point is somehow the church gets taken up and everybody else gets punished.”
chunks.text:
We’re going to talk today about the seventh trumpet, but before we get into that, I want to show you just some basic charts. There’s so many of them, but here’s the premillennial view. You have here the rapture. They have somehow taken Thessalonians and turned it into an ambiguous Jesus coming in the heavenly, snatching up the church and leaving again without revealing Himself to the whole world, very ambiguous. But here is this, quote unquote, rapture. They got the energy crisis down here like that’s supposed to mean something. And they got the temple being built, good God, help us. They got the seals, three and a half years. They got the beast, the antichrist, coming up. Then you got the trumpets, and the seventh trumpet is when everything ends, and then they got the vials being poured out, three and a half more years, and then they got the millennium. The problem they got here is there’s two witnesses here, as you’ll see later, are doing some very powerful things, okay? That’s a real problem with this chart, as you will see. You got the man-child and the man-child’s mother with three and a half years, both of these are three and a half years, and then you got the beast rising up for three and a half years. Well, it adds up to about 14 years, not seven.

Okay, here’s another chart, and, uh, you can see here’s three and a half years. Revelation 8:9 through 11:15, you got the seals, then you got the trumpet, then you got the seventh trumpet, and again you got this problem with the Gentiles treading the courts of the temple of God for three and a half years. All right, then you got the two witnesses bringing out fire from their mouth for three and a half years and tormenting the people on earth, and then you got the man-child’s mother in the wilderness for three and a half years, and then you got the beast for three and a half years. How many do that add up to? 14 years. Okay. Now, you know, people can write charts all they want to. What is their end goal? That’s what I want to know. And like an author who wrote this book, you know, when you read a book, you should know who the author is and what they’re trying to get across. See, what’s their point? The whole point is somehow the church gets taken up and everybody else gets punished. That’s their goal. Somehow we deserve to be raised up before the second coming.

Before the second coming. Then we got the amillennium people who say we, the whole thing is we’re reigning and ruling ever since Christ came, and then you got, I’m sorry, the amillennium, there is no millennium, and then you got the postmillennium people, and then the pre-tribulation rapture and the post-tribulation rapture and the mid-tribulation rapture and the prewrath rapture. chunks.section_question: Does God dwell in temples made with hands? (Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, Isaiah 66:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says “God does not dwell in temples made with hands,” citing Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24 and Isaiah 66:1. He says the Jewish temple was “a shadow of things to come” and “a pattern,” and God destroyed it because “the Jews couldn’t leave it,” just as we struggle to leave how we were raised to serve God.
chunks.text: Now, Acts 7, verse 48. This is what we know, we know this, ain’t no ifs and buts about it. We know this truth: God dwells not in temples made with hands. Says it in Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, and Isaiah 66:1. God does not dwell in temples made with hands. Well, why do we want to build a temple if God is dwelling, and temples made with hands? He already destroyed the Jewish temple that pointed to the church, the real temple of God. He had the Roman army destroy it because the Jews couldn’t leave it. And aren’t we like that today? We can’t leave how we were raised to serve God to really enter in to the fullness of God. Don’t we struggle with that? Yeah. So did the Jews, man. They worshiped that natural temple, and that natural temple, the Bible says, was plainly a shadow of things to come, doesn’t it say that? A pattern of what was to come.

This can open this Bible up to you when you read it. Now, if God has got a new Jerusalem, what do I care about Jerusalem over in Israel? Could that be an amen? chunks.section_question: Does God want to live in you rather than in a building? (Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16, 2 Corinthians 6:16)
chunks.short_answer: He says “a temple is an abiding place,” and God “wants to take up residence in your life.” He cites Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16 and 2 Corinthians 6:16, and says “I don’t have to wait for some natural temple to be built,” since “We have been the temple of God that He’s interested in.”
chunks.text:
He wants to live with you. A temple is an abiding place, a home is a place of residence, abiding place. He wants to take up residence in your life. Wow. Revelation 21:10: “He showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God.” “I saw no temple there, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.” See, they dwell there. “There will in no wise enter into it anything that defiles, neither whatsoever works an abomination or makes a lie, but they which are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” Folks, I don’t know about you, but the only way since Jesus came was to believe on Him for forgiveness of sin and get your name written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. This has been going on for 2,000 years, not three and a half. We have been the temple of God that He’s interested in. He got rid of the natural temple because He came and fulfilled what the natural temple pointed to and was a pattern of.

1 Corinthians 3:16: “You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you. If any man defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him, for the temple of God is holy, which temple you are.” So, see, I can’t defile my temple. I don’t have to wait for some natural temple to be built in some, and, I, Christ rise up and offer some kind of stupid sacrifice on it that they dream up. It’s not in the book. They dream this stuff up. 2 Corinthians 6:16: “You are the temple of the living God, as God has said: ‘I will dwell in them and walk in them, and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.’” Do we get it? See, we know God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He dwells with human beings that believe on Him. Amen. And us human beings are not to defile the temple.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal. Also she had a great and high wall with twelve gates, and twelve angels at the gates, and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: three gates on the east, three gates on the north, three gates on the south, and three gates on the west. Now the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. And he who talked with me had a gold reed to measure the city, its gates, and its wall. The city is laid out as a square; its length is as great as its breadth. And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand furlongs. Its length, breadth, and height are equal. Then he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of an angel. The construction of its wall was of jasper; and the city was pure gold, like clear glass. The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with all kinds of precious stones: the first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, the fifth sardonyx, the sixth sardius, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. The twelve gates were twelve pearls: each individual gate was of one pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass. But I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light. And the nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and honor into it. Its gates shall not be shut at all by day (there shall be no night there). And they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it. But there shall by no means enter it anything that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.
Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell in them And walk among them. I will be their God, And they shall be My people.”

chunks.section_question: Who are the two witnesses in Revelation 11? (Revelation 11:3-4)
chunks.short_answer: He says the two witnesses prophesy for three and a half years, with fire coming out of their mouths. He lists guesses that they are Moses and Elijah, or John the Baptist and Jesus, or “two prophets to come,” and notes the two olive trees and two lampstands (Revelation 11:4, Zechariah 4:14), but says “all these are great speculations.”
chunks.text:
Amen. Hallelujah. We are that new Jerusalem. We’re free, and there’s no temple in it because Christ, when He comes and dwells in us, is the temple. Hallelujah. Then in Revelation 11:3, there are two prophets, two witnesses, that rise up and begin to prophesy for three and a half years. Okay, fire comes out of their mouth, the Bible says, and destroys anybody that messes around with them. He says it kills them. I mean, these two guys are going around, you talk about a dragon. And the Bible says they tormented the people on earth for three and a half years. You young people, there is a time coming up the road where God’s going to manifest Himself, and you’re going to be glad you chose Christ when that happens. I mean, these two witnesses are something else.

“I will give power unto my two witnesses for three and a half years.” Now, the Bible says in Acts 1:8 that we are the witnesses of God, “You shall be My witnesses.” In Isaiah 43:10 it says Israel was a witness for God. Some say Moses and Elijah are the two witnesses, and some of us just say these are two prophets to come, we’ve never seen anything like them. Some people say it’s John the Baptist and Jesus, which prophesied and spoke for three and a half years, and then John rose with Jesus when all the saints of old rose, and all these are great speculations. In verse 4 of Revelation 11, it says these are two olive trees and two lampstands standing before the God of the earth. Now, do you remember what the lampstand is? What’s the lampstand? The church. Okay, so two churches. Hm. The church of Israel in the wilderness, the church of Jesus Christ. Okay, the two olive trees are two anointed ones that stand beside the Lord of the whole earth. In Zechariah 4:14 it talks about one lampstand and two olive trees. Okay, so some say it’s one lampstand because the Jews and Gentiles are one church. Now, the problem with all the above, all that I said, is this.

I mean, these two witnesses are something else.

chunks.section_question: Could the two witnesses be Moses and Elijah, or Jesus and John the Baptist? (Revelation 11:5)
chunks.short_answer: He says “Jesus didn’t spit fire out, neither did John the Baptist,” and “no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them.” He says “it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah, and it’s definitely not anyone that we have ever heard about in history.”
chunks.text: “If anyone wants to harm these two witnesses, fire proceeds from their mouth and destroys their enemies.” Jesus didn’t spit fire out, neither did John the Baptist. They let their enemies kill them, both of them did, so it’s definitely not them, is it? And it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah, and it’s definitely not anyone that we have ever heard about in history. Could that be an amen? Because no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them and tormenting people. These two prophets are tormenting the people of the world, torturing them. Okay, so that eliminates all the theories. Could that be an amen? Could that be an amen?

chunks.section_question: What power do the two witnesses have, and is the beast the antichrist? (Revelation 11:6-7)
chunks.short_answer: He says they have power to shut up heaven and turn waters to blood, like the seals and trumpets. He says “this leaves Israel and the church out,” since neither has done these things since Jesus left, and “nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.”
chunks.text: Absolutely. “These have power to shut up heaven so that no rainfall falls in the days of their prophecy, and they have power over the waters to turn them into blood and strike the earth with all plagues as often as they desire.” And if you remember the seals and the trumpets, that’s what was going on: fire, blood, all this stuff. So it’s almost like a connection here. “As often as they want,” they bring these plagues. So this leaves Israel and the church out, unless the church is empowered in the last days to do these things, because neither Israel nor God’s church since Jesus left this earth has done these things. Am I right? Absolutely. “The beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war with these and overcome them and kill them.” And nowhere in the Bible, church, does it say the beast is the antichrist. See, they have to connect it with their own human intellect. Nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.

chunks.section_question: Where do the two witnesses die, and how can everyone see them? (Revelation 11:7-12)
chunks.short_answer: He says Sodom and Egypt are Old Testament metaphors for Jerusalem, and the bodies are seen by all peoples while the world rejoices. He asks how everyone could see them and says “trying to literally interpret it as natural things in sequence just doesn’t work,” just as “everybody on earth sees Jesus when He comes,” because “He just opens your eyes to see.”
chunks.text:
“He makes war against them and kills them, and they lay for three days in the streets of Jerusalem, called Sodom and Egypt.” That’s a metaphor in the Old Testament of Jerusalem, “where the Lord was crucified.” So these guys are supposed to actually lie in the natural city of Jerusalem somewhere? We’ve never read it in history, have we? No. For three and a half years? Hm, interesting. “Then those from the peoples, the tongues, the tribes, the nations will see their dead bodies three and a half days and not allow their dead bodies to be put into the grave, and all those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, make merry, and send gifts to one another” (Christmas time) “because these two prophets who tormented those on earth are dead.” They’re happy these guys are gone. Now let me ask you this question: how can everybody see these two prophets? You say, “Well, the satellite TV.” Yeah, but not everybody has one. “Well, we got Internet.” Not everybody has a computer. Let me ask you this: how did they see Jesus? Everybody on earth sees Jesus when He comes. Does God need a satellite TV to do that? No, He just opens your eyes to see. Am I giving you food for thought? See, trying to literally interpret it as natural things in sequence just doesn’t work, and when it doesn’t work, we just need to leave it alone until He, what? Opens our eyes and we understand.

“After three and a half days, life comes back into them, they stood on their feet, and a great fear fell on those who saw them, and they heard a loud voice from heaven saying, ‘Come up here,’ and they ascended to heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.” All their enemies saw them ascend. Now, to me, that’s not too hard to figure out, but I’m going to leave that for you. When Jesus comes, does everybody see Him? Will everybody see the graves open and the people arise? Yeah. Why? Because He’s going to, He’s going to open your eyes to see Him. Because see, in the natural mind, if Jesus came in America, how would China see Him? But see, He’s coming all over the earth. He’s God, and people are going to witness this event. It says every eye sees Him. It’s not some rapture where everybody’s going, “What happened? Huh? What happened?” No, we all, what? See. Amen. Hallelujah.

chunks.short_answer: He says it “doesn’t make sense” for 7,000 to be killed in a city of millions “unless you know the Scriptures about 7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee.” He says the remnant “were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven,” and “you’re going to see that we are the remnant.”
chunks.text: “Now there was a great earthquake the same hour, a tenth of the city fell in the earthquake, 7,000 people were killed.” Why 7,000? Why 7,000? A great earthquake, there’s millions of people in the city of Jerusalem, and 7,000 are killed. Doesn’t make sense unless you know the Scriptures about 7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee. So these 7,000 were bowing their knee, but anyway, “and the remnant,” listen, the remnant, that’s coming up later, “were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven.” The remnant, the remainder of the people, were afraid. They were in fear, respect, and they, what? Honor God. And you’re going to see that we are the remnant in a few minutes. Hallelujah. “The second woe is past, the third woe is coming.” Okay, are you with me so far? These are three and a half and three and a half. Is how many years? Seven. Now, we got the abomination of desolation, Daniel, that they stretch over 49 weeks. They take one week and stretch it over to the end time. They have it, and it fits right in. I’ve calculated it out from the carrying away to the building of the temple when Jesus came was about the years. It’s very close. Now, let me ask you this: when did the sacrifices cease, the abomination of desolation spoken by Daniel the prophet?

chunks.section_question: When did the sacrifices cease, and what is the abomination of desolation? (Daniel 9:27, Matthew 24:15, Luke 21:20)
chunks.short_answer: He says the sacrifices ceased not when the temple was torn down but “when Jesus died on the cross… He fulfilled all the law, all those types and shadows and patterns.” He compares Matthew’s “abomination of desolation” with Luke’s “Jerusalem surrounded by armies,” says “the abomination of desolation has happened,” and says “nowhere does it say there’s seven years of tribulation.”
chunks.text:
See that the sacrifices will cease. Okay, now remember we told you, in Matthew it says, “When you see the abomination of desolation,” then flee to the mountains for the destruction of Jerusalem is coming. But in Luke, he doesn’t say, he does say “abomination of desolation,” he says, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, flee to the mountain, for its destruction is coming.” And so the abomination of desolation has happened. Right now, let me ask you this: when did the sacrifices cease? Was it when the temple was torn down? No, it’s when Jesus died on the cross. Right. When He died, there was no more sacrifices. He did it. See, He fulfilled all the prophecies, He fulfilled all the law, all those types and shadows and patterns. He did it all. And so when He died, and He said, “It is finished,” that’s when the sacrifices were finished. Did the Jews keep sacrificing? Yes. Did it mean they had any profit, any clout? No. Why? Because Jesus, the one and only sacrifice, was done now, and our faith was to be in Him, and all sacrifices were to, what? Cease.

And so the Jews couldn’t get out of the natural, just like we can’t get out of the natural, and so God had the Roman army come in and destroy the temple, so now they can’t sacrifice. Why? And if you don’t want to get out of the natural and into the spiritual, God has ways to fix you. I tell you, take the faith way, take the believing way. Don’t take that other way. That’s a tough road to hoe. Hallelujah. Amen. What’s the one sacrifice left that we do? Praise. “The sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks unto His name,” which most Christians will not do. Why? Because of the way they were raised, the way they were taught. Are you with me? Now, let’s continue. Revelation 12:6, we’re going to get into this, but there’s a woman who has fled in the wilderness for three and a half years that birth the man-child. Okay, and then in Revelation 13:5 we got the dragon and the beast warring with the saints and winning, for how long? Three and a half years. Church, there’s a lot of three and a half years here, and nowhere does it say there’s seven years of tribulation. It’s not there. In one sentence, it’s not there. You have to add all this stuff up, twist Scriptures, rubber band them over here and there. Are you with me?

Yeah. Is He the King of kings and Lord of lords of the nations now? Yeah. Duh. Hallelujah. Matthew 28:18: “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth. chunks.short_answer: He says the nations being angry, the dead being judged and the saints being rewarded are “all happening at the same time.” He says “the third woe… doesn’t sound like much of a woe to me when you’re on the right side,” and that resurrection and judgment are described together in the passage.
chunks.text: He says, “You have taken Your great power and reign.” “The nations were angry, for Your wrath has come, and the time of the dead that are judged, and the rewards for the saints.” Look at this. Everything is happening at the same time. Watch this, just read it. The nations are what? Do they, a lot of the people, nations means people, are a lot of people mad at Jesus? They don’t like you saying that name. Is our government mad at Jesus? They don’t want the name said. Yeah. “Your wrath has come.” Okay, these plagues, these things that God does to get people’s attention and get them to repent, as we learn. “And the time of the dead being judged.” Oh, how does the dead get judged? faqs.question: What does he say is the problem with the prophecy charts?
faqs.answer: He says each chart has several periods of three and a half years that “adds up to about 14 years, not seven,” and that the two witnesses are “a real problem with this chart.”

faqs.question: What does he say about a temple being rebuilt?
faqs.answer: He says “the natural temple was destroyed in 70 AD,” so “he’s not talking about measuring that temple, is he? No.” He says people want a rebuilt temple “because they’re trying to reduce this down to a natural temple.”

faqs.question: Does God live in buildings made by people?
faqs.answer: He says no: “God does not dwell in temples made with hands.” He says the real temple is the church and the Jewish temple “pointed to the church, the real temple of God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says:

faqs.question: Why does he ask where Mount Sinai is?
faqs.answer: He says Galatians says Hagar is Mount Sinai “in Arabia,” and asks Bible scholars, “could it be that the maps are wrong and Mount Sinai is actually in another place that the maps haven’t told us?” He says he is “just throwing that out.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: for this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children— but the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all.

faqs.question: What does he mean by “the new Jerusalem”?
faqs.answer: He says “we are come to… the new Jerusalem, the church,” and “He’s after you. He’s interested in you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name.

faqs.question: What is a temple, according to him?
faqs.answer: He says “a temple is an abiding place, a home is a place of residence, abiding place. He wants to take up residence in your life.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal. Also she had a great and high wall with twelve gates, and twelve angels at the gates, and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: three gates on the east, three gates on the north, three gates on the south, and three gates on the west. Now the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. And he who talked with me had a gold reed to measure the city, its gates, and its wall. The city is laid out as a square; its length is as great as its breadth. And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand furlongs. Its length, breadth, and height are equal. Then he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of an angel. The construction of its wall was of jasper; and the city was pure gold, like clear glass. The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with all kinds of precious stones: the first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, the fifth sardonyx, the sixth sardius, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. The twelve gates were twelve pearls: each individual gate was of one pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass. But I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light. And the nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and honor into it. Its gates shall not be shut at all by day (there shall be no night there). And they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it. But there shall by no means enter it anything that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.

faqs.question: Can a Christian defile the temple of God?
faqs.answer: He says yes, in the sense that “us human beings are not to defile the temple,” since “you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

faqs.question: How long do the two witnesses prophesy?
faqs.answer: He says “for three and a half years,” with fire coming out of their mouths, and they “tormented the people on earth.” He says to the young people that God is going to manifest Himself and “you’re going to be glad you chose Christ when that happens.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I will give power to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.” These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the God of the earth.

faqs.question: Why does he say the two witnesses are not Moses and Elijah?
faqs.answer: He says “no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them,” and “it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouth and devours their enemies. And if anyone wants to harm them, he must be killed in this manner.

faqs.question: Does the Bible say the beast is the antichrist?
faqs.answer: He says “nowhere in the Bible, church, does it say the beast is the antichrist.” He adds, “Nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: These have power to shut heaven, so that no rain falls in the days of their prophecy; and they have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to strike the earth with all plagues, as often as they desire. When they finish their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them.

faqs.question: How can everyone on earth see the two witnesses?
faqs.answer: He says it is the same as everyone seeing Jesus when He comes: “does God need a satellite TV to do that? No, He just opens your eyes to see.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: When they finish their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. Then those from the peoples, tribes, tongues, and nations will see their dead bodies three-and-a-half days, and not allow their dead bodies to be put into graves. And those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, make merry, and send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth. Now after the three-and-a-half days the breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who saw them. And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, “Come up here.” And they ascended to heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.

faqs.question: Why were 7,000 people killed in the earthquake?
faqs.answer: He says it “doesn’t make sense” for “millions of people in the city” unless you know of “7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: In the same hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. In the earthquake seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven. The second woe is past. Behold, the third woe is coming quickly.

faqs.question: When does he say the sacrifices ceased?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s when Jesus died on the cross. Right. When He died, there was no more sacrifices.” and when He said “It is finished,” that is “when the sacrifices were finished.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week; But in the middle of the week He shall bring an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of abominations shall be one who makes desolate, Even until the consummation, which is determined, Is poured out on the desolate.”

faqs.question: What sacrifice does he say is left for believers?
faqs.answer: He says “the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks unto His name,” which “most Christians will not do” because of the way they were raised.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.

faqs.question: Is Christ reigning now?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “Is He the King of kings and Lord of lords of the nations now? Yeah.” He cites “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.
